elements.quote: Methods We searched PubMed, Web of Science, Medline, Embase, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, China National Knowledge Infrastructure, and Wanfang for cohort studies, case-control studies, and cross-sectional studies up to March 16, 2023, to conduct a meta-analysis of global SARS-CoV-2 reinfection rate.
elements.reason: The abstract identifies the study as a meta-analysis but does not explicitly use the phrase 'systematic review' in the abstract text provided.

elements.quote: Methods We searched PubMed, Web of Science, Medline, Embase, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, China National Knowledge Infrastructure, and Wanfang for cohort studies, case-control studies, and cross-sectional studies up to March 16, 2023, to conduct a meta-analysis of global SARS-CoV-2 reinfection rate.
elements.reason: The abstract explicitly states the objective to conduct a meta-analysis of global SARS-CoV-2 reinfection rate.

elements.quote: Methods We searched PubMed, Web of Science, Medline, Embase, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, China National Knowledge Infrastructure, and Wanfang for cohort studies, case-control studies, and cross-sectional studies up to March 16, 2023
elements.reason: The abstract specifies inclusion criteria regarding study design (cohort, case-control, cross-sectional) but does not explicitly list exclusion criteria.

elements.quote: Methods We searched PubMed, Web of Science, Medline, Embase, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, China National Knowledge Infrastructure, and Wanfang for cohort studies, case-control studies, and cross-sectional studies up to March 16, 2023
elements.reason: The abstract identifies the information sources (databases) and the date the search was last conducted (March 16, 2023).

elements.quote: The risk of bias was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale and the Joanna Briggs Institute critical appraisal tool.
elements.reason: The abstract specifies the methods used to assess risk of bias (Newcastle-Ottawa Scale and Joanna Briggs Institute).

elements.quote: Subgroup analyses were performed for age, country, study type, and study population, and time-varying reinfection rates of SARS-CoV-2 were estimated using meta-regression.
elements.reason: The abstract specifies the methods used to present and synthesize results (subgroup analyses, meta-regression).

elements.quote: Result A total of 55 studies involving 111,846 cases of SARS-CoV-2 reinfection were included.
elements.reason: The abstract reports the total number of included studies (55) and participants/cases (111,846).

elements.quote: The pooled SARSCoV-2 reinfection rate was 0.94% (95% CI : 0.65 -1.35%).
elements.reason: The abstract presents results for the main outcome (pooled reinfection rate) with the number of included studies and participants.

elements.quote: The pooled SARSCoV-2 reinfection rate was 0.94% (95% CI : 0.65 -1.35%).
elements.reason: The abstract reports the summary estimate (0.94%) and its 95% confidence interval.

elements.quote: SARS-CoV-2 is at risk of reinfection and the Omicron variant has a higher reinfection rate than other currently known variants.
elements.reason: The abstract indicates the direction of effect (higher) and which group is favored (Omicron variant) when comparing variants.
The abstract does not summarize important limitations of the included evidence; limitations are reported in the main text (text_19).

elements.quote: Conclusion Meta-regression analysis found that the overall reinfection rate increased and then decreased over time... The results of this study could help guide public health measures and vaccination strategies in response to the Coronavirus Disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic.
elements.reason: The abstract provides a general interpretation of the results and their implications for public health measures.
The abstract does not specify the primary source of funding; funding is reported in the main text (text_19).
The abstract does not provide the register name and registration number; registration is reported in the main text (text_6).

elements.quote: Therefore, the aim of this study was to conduct a meta-analysis to describe and summarize the current reinfection rates in different regions and among diverse populations. Furthermore, the study sought to examine trends in reinfection rates over time, so as to provide reference for the development of global unified reinfection standards and reinfection measures in the future.
elements.reason: The manuscript explicitly states the study's aims and objectives in the text.

elements.quote: Therefore, the aim of this study was to conduct a meta-analysis to describe and summarize the current reinfection rates in different regions and among diverse populations.
elements.reason: This is a systematic review of observational data regarding reinfection rates, not an intervention review. Therefore, the requirement to state planned comparisons using PICO for intervention effects does not apply.

elements.quote: The inclusion criteria were: (1) Conformed to research questions, i.e., studies that estimated the reinfection rate of SARS-CoV-2 or we could calculate it based on the data provided in the paper; (2) The study design included cohort study, case-control study, and descriptive study; (3) The study fited our working definition of SARS-CoV-2 reinfection... reinfection working definition in this study was based on a positive laboratory result at least 90 days after laboratory confirmation of primary infection... (4) Original research.
elements.reason: The manuscript explicitly specifies study designs, research question alignment, follow-up requirements (90-day definition), and original research status as eligibility criteria.

elements.quote: To avoid language bias, the search was not limited to any language. ... The exclusion criteria were: ... (4) Grey literature...
elements.reason: Language and publication/report status (original research vs grey literature) are specified, but dissemination year is not mentioned in the eligibility criteria.
The manuscript excludes studies with unreported numbers but does not explicitly distinguish between exclusions due to outcomes not being measured versus outcomes not reported.

elements.quote: Subgroup analyses were performed by meta-regression to fit stratified rates of reinfection based on variables such as variant and country... We constructed a multiple meta-regression using the time interval between two positive tests as the independent variable...
elements.reason: The review specifies groups used for synthesis (variant, country, time interval) and links them to the review objectives regarding trends and regional differences.

elements.quote: Therefore, the aim of this study was to conduct a meta-analysis to describe and summarize the current reinfection rates... reinfection working definition in this study was based on a positive laboratory result at least 90 days after laboratory confirmation... advised from WHO and US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention [21, 22]. ... In order to avoid data heterogeneity in metaanalysis while ensuring data quantity, we used previous literature and previous definitions of reinfection in some countries as the criteria for included literature...
elements.reason: Rationales are provided for the specific reinfection definition (to account for time trends and heterogeneity) and the exclusion of grey literature.

elements.quote: from January 1, 2020 to March 16, 2023
elements.reason: The text explicitly states the search date range, indicating the last search date was March 16, 2023.

elements.quote: We searched for papers published on PubMed, Web of Science, Medline(Ovid), Embase(Ovid), Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, China National Knowledge Infrastructure(CNKI), Wanfang
elements.reason: Database names and search interfaces (Ovid) are reported, but available coverage dates of the databases are not explicitly stated (only the search date range for papers is given).

elements.quote: Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials... from January 1, 2020 to March 16, 2023
elements.reason: The name of the register is reported, and the search date range is provided, though specific date restrictions for the register itself are not distinguished from the search date range.
No websites, search engines, or other online sources were reported as searched in the retrieved evidence.
No organisations or manufacturers were reported as contacted to identify studies.
No types of individuals contacted to identify studies were described.
No reference lists were reported as examined for study identification.
No backward or forward citation searching was reported.
No journals or conference proceedings were reported as consulted directly.

elements.quote: We searched for papers published on PubMed, Web of Science, Medline(Ovid), Embase(Ovid), Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, China National Knowledge Infrastructure(CNKI), Wanfang using 'COVID-19' , '2019-nCoV' , 'SARS-COV-2' , 'Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus 2' , 'reinfection' , 'recurrence' , 'repeat positive' and 'repeat infections' as keywords, from January 1, 2020 to March 16, 2023 (Additional file 2).
elements.reason: Databases and keywords are listed, but the complete search strategy (Boolean logic, field tags) is referenced in supplementary material (Additional file 2) which is not included in the retrieved evidence.

elements.quote: To avoid language bias, the search was not limited to any language.
elements.reason: Language limit is described and justified ('To avoid language bias'). Date limit is described but justification is not explicit. Other limits in supplementary material are not visible.

elements.quote: The search strategy we used was based on previous studies
elements.reason: Mentions strategy was based on previous studies but does not cite specific published search approaches or describe adaptations in the text.
No mention of natural-language processing or text-analysis tools used for search terms.
Google Translate is mentioned for article translation, not for translating search strings between sources.
No description of search strategy validation process or studies.
No description of peer review of the search strategy (e.g., PRESS).
No description of search structure development or indication if PICO was not used.

elements.quote: The reviewers independently (CY, Z-WH, H-XY, C-MS, LX, H-HP) screened the literature based on inclusion and exclusion criteria.
elements.reason: The text lists the reviewers but does not specify the number of reviewers who screened each record or report (e.g., 'two reviewers').

elements.quote: The reviewers independently (CY, Z-WH, H-XY, C-MS, LX, H-HP) screened the literature based on inclusion and exclusion criteria.
elements.reason: The manuscript explicitly states that reviewers screened the literature independently.

elements.quote: Conflicts were resolved by other independent reviewers (ZT Y-CH).
elements.reason: The manuscript describes the process for resolving conflicts/disagreements involving other independent reviewers.
There is no mention of processes used to obtain or confirm eligibility information from study investigators.

elements.quote: ...if the included article was neither in English nor in Chinese and did not provide an English abstract or full text, we used an online translator (Google Translate) for translation.
elements.reason: The manuscript reports using an online translator (Google Translate) for eligible articles not in English or Chinese.
There is no description of automation tools integrated into the selection process.

elements.quote: Records removed before screening: Duplicate records removed (n=10224)
elements.reason: While the flow diagram reports records removed before screening, it does not identify externally derived classifiers by version or reference.
There is no description of internally derived classifiers, their use, training, or validation.
There is no description of machine-learning prioritisation tools or screening stopping rules.
There is no description of crowdsourcing platforms.
There is no description of previously screened datasets used to eliminate records.

elements.quote: Risk bias assessment was performed by two independent reviewers (H-XY, C-MS)
elements.reason: Reports the number of reviewers (two) performing risk bias assessment, which constitutes data collection.

elements.quote: The reviewers independently (CY, Z-WH, H-XY, C-MS, LX, H-HP) screened the literature
elements.reason: Explicitly states that reviewers worked independently during screening and risk bias assessment.

elements.quote: Conflicts were resolved by other independent reviewers (ZT Y-CH)
elements.reason: Describes the process for resolving disagreements between data collectors.
No mention of processes used to obtain or confirm data from study investigators.

elements.quote: we used an online translator (Google Translate) for translation
elements.reason: Mentions use of an automation tool (Google Translate) for translation, but does not describe training or validation.

elements.quote: we used an online translator (Google Translate) for translation
elements.reason: Explicitly reports the method used to translate articles for data collection.
No specification of software used to extract data from figures.

elements.quote: selected one of two literature with the same population for inclusion
elements.reason: Describes decision rules for selecting data when multiple reports covered the same population.

elements.quote: The complete information extracted included the first author, study period, country, study population, sample size, study design, reinfected variants, time between two positive tests (days), age, reinfection rate, and the number of reinfections.
elements.reason: The manuscript explicitly lists the data items/outcomes sought (including reinfection rate and number of reinfections) and provides a definition for reinfection ('positive laboratory result at least 90 days after laboratory confirmation').

elements.quote: The complete information extracted included the first author, study period, country, study population, sample size, study design, reinfected variants, time between two positive tests (days), age, reinfection rate, and the number of reinfections.
elements.reason: The 'study period' is explicitly listed as an extracted data item, specifying the time frame context for the outcome measurements.

elements.quote: The complete information extracted included the first author, study period, country, study population, sample size, study design, reinfected variants, time between two positive tests (days), age, reinfection rate, and the number of reinfections.
elements.reason: The phrase 'complete information extracted' indicates that all compatible results within the outcome domains were sought.

The authors state they extracted 'complete information', implying all compatible results were sought; therefore, the conditional requirement to describe selection processes for unsought results does not apply.
There is no explicit report of changes to outcome-domain inclusion, definitions, or importance compared to a protocol, although standardization strategies are mentioned.
There is no explicit report of changes to processes for selecting results within eligible outcome domains.

elements.quote: Therefore, the aim of this study was to conduct a meta-analysis to describe and summarize the current reinfection rates in different regions and among diverse populations. Furthermore, the study sought to examine trends in reinfection rates over time... previous meta-analysis only performed subgroup analysis... and the reinfection rate was a fixed value. The time trend of the reinfection rate is not clear
elements.reason: The manuscript identifies the examination of time trends as a key aim with a rationale (previous studies missed this), indicating prioritization, but lacks a dedicated section explicitly ranking outcomes.

elements.quote: The complete information extracted included the first author, study period, country, study population, sample size, study design, reinfected variants, time between two positive tests (days), age, reinfection rate, and the number of reinfections.
elements.reason: The manuscript explicitly lists all variables for which data were sought in the 'Selection Criteria And Data Extraction' section.

elements.quote: If the paper did not mention the reinfection variant, we classified the reinfection variants based on the WHO standards according to the study period.
elements.reason: The manuscript describes the assumption/procedure used when specific study information (reinfection variant) was missing.

elements.quote: Additional file 3: Information extraction form.
elements.reason: The Supplementary Information section lists an 'Information extraction form' as Additional file 3, indicating a tool was used to determine data items.

elements.quote: We used the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale (NOS) to evaluate the literature quality of cohort and case-control studies, and the Joanna Briggs Institute critical appraisal tool (JBI) for cross-sectional studies
elements.reason: The specific risk-of-bias tools (NOS and JBI) are clearly named in the text.
The text mentions the tools but refers to 'Additional file 4' for details and does not list the specific domains, components, or items assessed within the provided text.

elements.quote: When the star rating in NOS was less than 3, or the number of 'yes' in JBI was less than 5 [23], we categorized the paper as 'high risk of bias'
elements.reason: The text specifies the rule used to derive the overall risk-of-bias judgement (categorization as 'high risk of bias').
No adaptations to the existing risk-of-bias tools are described in the retrieved evidence.
No newly developed risk-of-bias tool is described in the retrieved evidence.

elements.quote: Risk bias assessment was performed by two independent reviewers (H-XY, C-MS), and inconsistencies were judged by other independent reviewers (CY, Z-WH)
elements.reason: The text specifies the number of reviewers (two), their independence, and the procedure for resolving disagreements (judged by other independent reviewers).
No processes used to obtain or confirm risk-of-bias information from study investigators are described in the retrieved evidence.
No automation tools used for risk-of-bias assessment are described in the retrieved evidence.

elements.quote: We used meta-analysis to evaluate the pooled rate of SARS-CoV-2 reinfection in the included studies... we decided to use the logit transformation
elements.reason: The text explicitly specifies the effect measure as the 'pooled rate' and notes the use of 'logit transformation' for the synthesis.
The retrieved evidence does not report any thresholds or ranges used to interpret the effect size (reinfection rate) or the rationale for them.
While the text describes transforming the rate for analysis, it does not explicitly describe the method used to re-express the synthesized results back to the original rate scale.

elements.quote: However, when the rate is close to 0 or 1, two problems will occur in the meta-regression: the confidence interval may exceed the interval of 0-1, and the variance is squeezed towards 0. Therefore, we converted the reinfection rate to an approximate normal distribution.
elements.reason: The text provides a justification for the choice of transformation (logit) to address statistical issues with rates close to 0 or 1, which supports the choice of effect measure handling.

elements.quote: The inclusion criteria were: (1) Conformed to research questions, i.e., studies that estimated the reinfection rate of SARS-CoV-2 or we could calculate it based on the data provided in the paper; (2) The study design included cohort study, case-control study, and descriptive study; (3) The study fited our working definition of SARS-CoV-2 reinfection... (4) Original research... The complete information extracted included the first author, study period, country, study population, sample size, study design, reinfected variants, time between two positive tests (days), age, reinfection rate, and the number of reinfections... If the paper did not mention the reinfection variant, we classified the reinfection variants based on the WHO standards according to the study period.
elements.reason: The manuscript explicitly details the inclusion criteria for the review and the data extraction process, including specific rules for classifying reinfection variants, which determines eligibility for the respective subgroup syntheses.

elements.quote: Therefore, we converted the reinfection rate to an approximate normal distribution. Four transformations were taken: log transformation, logit transformation, arcsine transformation, and double arcsine transformation. Through the hypothesis test after the transformation, we decided to use the logit transformation (see Additional file 5 for specific results).
elements.reason: The Statistical Method section explicitly describes the data conversion methods (specifically the logit transformation chosen from four options) used to prepare the reinfection rates for meta-analysis, satisfying the requirement to describe methods for data preparation.

elements.quote: Subgroup analyses were performed for age, reinfection variant, country, study population, and study type respectively, and the results were shown in Table 1
elements.reason: The text explicitly describes the tabular structure (Table 1) and the data included within it (subgroup analysis results for various factors).

elements.quote: Fig. 5 Meta-regression of time-varying reinfection rates among health care workers (red dots indicate true values, shaded areas are 95% CI )
elements.reason: The text describes the graphical methods used (meta-regression plot) and details the visual components (red dots, shaded areas).

elements.quote: Subgroup analyses were performed for age, reinfection variant, country, study population, and study type respectively
elements.reason: The text reports the specific basis for ordering or grouping studies within the tables (age, variant, country, etc.).
The manuscript uses standard graphical methods (forest plots, flow charts, meta-regression) and does not mention using non-standard graphs, so the rationale for non-standard graphs does not apply.

elements.quote: All analyses were performed using R statistical software (version 4.2.3).
elements.reason: Software and version number are reported, but specific statistical packages (e.g., metafor, meta) are not explicitly named.

elements.quote: We used meta-analysis to evaluate the pooled rate of SARS-CoV-2 reinfection in the included studies.
elements.reason: Meta-analysis was performed for the included studies, so the condition for alternative synthesis methods does not apply.

elements.quote: If heterogeneity was low, a fixed-effects model was used to combine rates and correction estimates from different studies. Otherwise, a random-effects model was used.
elements.reason: The choice between fixed-effects and random-effects models is described based on heterogeneity assessment.

elements.quote: Heterogeneity between studies was expressed using Cochran's Q statistic test ( P < 0.05) as well as I 2 > 50%... we constructed a multiple meta-regression... we also used spline regression...
elements.reason: Statistical methods including heterogeneity tests, meta-analysis models, meta-regression, and spline regression are described.

elements.quote: Heterogeneity between studies was expressed using Cochran's Q statistic test ( P < 0.05) as well as I 2 > 50%.
elements.reason: Methods to identify and quantify heterogeneity (Cochran's Q, I2) are explicitly reported.
While a random-effects model is mentioned, the specific between-study variance estimator (e.g., DerSimonian-Laird, REML) is not reported.
The method used to calculate confidence intervals (e.g., normal approximation, profile likelihood) is not described.
No other relevant random-effects implementation details (e.g., specific R packages, convergence criteria) are reported.
No Bayesian meta-analysis was performed or described in the manuscript.
No statistical method to account for dependency among multiple estimates from the same study is described; duplicate studies were excluded instead.

elements.quote: One of them reported only the reinfection rate, but not the associated number of first infections as well as the number of reinfections, and two other articles studied the same population, so the meta-analysis of single-group rates could not be performed. Therefore, we excluded the above literature...
elements.reason: Planned syntheses judged impossible (due to unreported data or same population) are identified with reasons for exclusion.

elements.quote: Subgroup analyses were performed by meta-regression to fit stratified rates of reinfection based on variables such as variant and country
elements.reason: The manuscript explicitly describes the methods used to explore heterogeneity, including subgroup analyses and meta-regression based on specific variables.

elements.quote: Subgroup analyses were performed for age, reinfection variant, country, study population, and study type respectively... After dividing the reinfection variants according to the time of reinfection reported in the literature, the reinfection rate of SARS-CoV-2 was 0.59%... for Alpha variants; 0.26%... for Wild variants
elements.reason: Factors (age, variant, country, etc.) and factor levels (Alpha, Wild, etc.) are reported, but the expected direction of effect modification is not explicitly stated as a pre-specified hypothesis.

elements.quote: Subgroup analyses were performed by meta-regression to fit stratified rates of reinfection based on variables such as variant and country
elements.reason: The text describes using meta-regression with variables like variant and country, which implies study-level variables, but does not explicitly state whether study-level variables, within-study contrasts, or both were used.

elements.quote: the difference in reinfection rate among different variants was statistically significant
elements.reason: The manuscript reports that differences were statistically significant but does not explicitly name the specific method used to compare subgroup effects (e.g., interaction test, Q-test for subgroup differences).
The manuscript does not describe any informal methods used to explore heterogeneity when meta-analysis was unsuitable; it focuses on meta-regression and spline regression.
The manuscript does not identify any analyses of heterogeneity that were not pre-specified as such.

elements.quote: However, the limitations of this study are as follows: first, we did not include the 'grey literature' , which may lack potential relevant studies that meet the inclusion criteria [35]. In addition, the pattern of publication bias in the field of single-arm study with single-group rate is not clear, and funnel plot analysis may lead to inaccurate conclusions. Second, there is still no clear global definition of SARS-CoV-2 reinfection. In the literature of reinfection searched in this study, most of the diagnostic criteria were at least 90 days between two positive laboratory tests. In order to avoid data heterogeneity in metaanalysis while ensuring data quantity, we used previous literature and previous definitions of reinfection in some countries as the criteria for included literature and data extraction in this study. Although we noted that clinical symptoms and real time-PCR or Rapid Antigen test were also important for the definition of SARS-CoV-2 reinfection, forming a globally harmonized standard definition was definitely beyond the scope of this study. Besides, due to the lack of specific data in the included literature, subgroup analysis of disease severity and vaccination could not be carried out, so it was impossible to explore all the sources of heterogeneity of SARS-CoV-2 reinfection rates. Meanwhile, the sample sizes of the literature included in this study were quite different, which might also be the source of heterogeneity in reinfection rates.
elements.reason: The manuscript explicitly discusses limitations of the evidence included in the review, including the exclusion of grey literature, publication bias concerns, lack of a global definition for reinfection, lack of data for subgroup analysis, and sample size heterogeneity, found in the Funding section.
